w10_T4_003302: A school received 12 tins of paint, and every tin was decanted into 3 glass jars. The jars were shared equally between 2 art rooms, and the upstairs room took one of those shares. A mural that covers 9 square metres used up 12 jars from the upstairs room. The jars still left there were divided equally among the 3 classes that use the room, and Class B took one share. Class B split its jars equally between 2 project groups, and the model-making group received one of the parts. The model-making group's cupboard already held 68 jars of paint. How many jars did the model-making group then have?
w10_T4_003309: Nadia had 151 empty photo frames in her studio and sold 55 of them at a market. Every frame she kept holds 6 photographs. Her colleague Peter frames photographs too, but he mounted fewer of them this year than Nadia did. The studio is 20 metres from the bus stop. Nadia later tripled the number of photographs she had mounted by working through an old archive. A gallery then bought 1531 of the photographs from her. How many photographs did Nadia still have?
w10_T4_003312: A recycling depot began the month with 222 crates of glass, and 106 crates went to the furnace straight away. Every crate that stayed was emptied into 3 smaller bins. The depot yard is 45 metres wide. A collection lorry took 278 of the bins away. The number of bins still at the depot was then tripled by a delivery of identical bins from a partner site, and a neighbour dropped off 50 more. How many bins were at the depot then?
w10_T4_003314: Sara bought 220 boxes of ceramic tiles, and each box holds 3 tiles. She used 285 tiles on the kitchen floor. The tiles that were left were shared equally between 3 rooms, and Sara kept the share meant for the hallway. She broke 37 of those hallway tiles while cutting them to size. The tiles still whole were arranged as 4 equal patches, and her brother Dan took charge of one patch, though Dan handled fewer tiles that day than Sara did. Dan's patch was later split into 2 equal parts for a repair, and only one of those parts was finished. How many tiles were in the part Dan finished?
w10_T4_003317: A repair cafe had 81 minutes of volunteer time booked for Saturday. A late volunteer added 27 minutes to the booking. Repairs during the morning used up 103 minutes of that time. The cafe has 14 workbenches in the hall. In the afternoon a new volunteer signed up for 64 minutes, and another added 37 minutes. The booking sheet is always kept in minutes, although the notice on the door advertises the session in hours. How many minutes of volunteer time did the booking sheet show at the end?
w10_T4_003319: A camping shop had 182 tent pegs in its stockroom. It sold 58 pegs on Friday and lost 33 more in a flooded box. A supplier sent 26 pegs, and a returned order added 20 others. A dozen of the pegs are the heavy steel kind used for winter camping. The shop van can carry 900 pegs at once. Every peg was then packed with 5 guy ropes to make a set, and 67 spare ropes found in a drawer were counted with them. How many guy ropes were counted?
w10_T4_003343: Kwame packs 139 tea bags into every carton at the factory. Each shipping box holds 6 cartons, and each pallet takes 3 shipping boxes. The factory canteen seats 75 people. Kwame's colleague Beatrice packed fewer tea bags than he did on the same shift. A quality check put 46 loose tea bags back onto the pallet, and a split carton added another 28. How many tea bags were on the pallet?
w10_T4_003347: Early on Sunday a bike hire kiosk had 143 helmets on its racks. Groups hired 135 helmets before lunch. In the early afternoon 17 helmets came back, and later a delivery brought 39 new ones. A dozen of the helmets are the small children's size. The kiosk stands 6 kilometres from the town centre. That evening the manager fitted every helmet in the kiosk with 9 replacement pads. How many replacement pads did the manager fit?
w10_T4_003352: A pottery studio started the term with 81 bags of clay. The beginners' class used 69 bags, and 8 more were ruined when they dried out. Each bag that remained was cut into 6 blocks, and every block makes 8 small bowls. A dozen of the bowls are glazed in blue for the shop window, and the kiln can fire 40 bowls at a time. The tutor then dropped 15 bowls before they could be fired. How many bowls survived?
w10_T4_003361: A wildlife group counted 224 nesting boxes across a woodland that covers 60 hectares. Half of the boxes stand on the north side, and the group surveyed that half only. Surveyors found 102 of the boxes they checked to be empty. Every box that was occupied held 4 chicks. Predators took 36 of those chicks over the following week. Each chick that survived was fitted with 3 coloured rings. How many coloured rings were used?
w10_T4_003365: Elif stitches 188 beads onto every bracelet she makes. Each gift box holds 4 bracelets, and each display tray holds 4 gift boxes. The craft fair she sells at runs for 6 hours. A wholesaler ordered 9 trays for each of the 7 shops in its chain. Elif's partner Hugo stitched fewer beads that month than Elif did, but he added 80 loose beads to the finished shipment. How many beads were in the shipment?
w10_T4_003367: A community centre had 231 chairs at the start of the season. 22 chairs were scrapped as broken, and a hall closure sent 54 more chairs to the centre. A dozen of the chairs are the padded sort kept for the committee room. Every chair takes 5 minutes to set out, and the caretaker added up the setup minutes for all of them. He records this work in minutes even though his timesheet is filled in with hours. He saved 777 minutes by using a trolley, and his colleague Ana added 15 minutes of her own, although Ana worked fewer minutes overall than he did. How many minutes did the setup finally come to?
w10_T4_003370: On Monday morning a school kitchen had 147 lunch trays ready. 45 trays were sent to the infants' block before break. At midday a delivery added 57 trays, and 3 trays were found cracked and were binned. In the afternoon the kitchen manager Rosa had every tray in the kitchen loaded with 8 items of cutlery, and the cutlery was counted. Her assistant Piet counted fewer items that day than Rosa did. In the evening 19 pieces of cutlery came back from the staff room and 26 from the sports hall, and both lots joined the count. How many pieces of cutlery were counted in all?
w10_T4_003377: A village shop had 46 sacks of flour in its store. 39 sacks were sold to a bakery. A mill then delivered 38 more sacks. A dozen of the sacks are the wholemeal kind. Every sack makes 5 loaves of bread. A neighbouring shop contributed 62 finished loaves to the same order. How many loaves were in the order?
w10_T4_003384: A garden club had 149 packets of seeds in its cupboard. Damp ruined 26 of the packets. A member donated 55 packets, and a seed swap brought in 16 more. A dozen of the packets hold sunflower seeds. The club meets in a hall that is 30 metres long. A late parcel then added 9 further packets. How many packets of seeds were in the cupboard?
w10_T4_003388: Dario loads 84 bricks onto each barrow at the building site. He fills 8 barrows to make one load. The site takes 5 such loads in a day, and the job ran for 5 days. Dario's workmate Yusra moved fewer bricks over that job than Dario did. Yusra added 21 spare bricks to Dario's tally at the end. How many bricks were in Dario's tally?
w10_T4_003396: A workshop had 171 sheets of plywood in stock and bought 23 more. Every sheet is cut into 4 panels, and each panel is sanded on 2 faces, with one sanding job counted for each face. Every sanding job uses 8 units of abrasive paper. The workshop times its jobs in minutes although the customer quotes are written in hours. The foreman Louis logged more sanding jobs than his apprentice Nina did, and the store room holds 300 sheets when full. How many units of abrasive paper does the whole run need?
w10_T4_003408: On Monday morning a seed factory filled 108 sachets in its first batch. By midday it had completed 9 such batches. During the afternoon 9 identical lines were running, each one matching that midday output. The factory keeps 24 forklifts on site. In the evening the manager confirmed that 9 factories in the group had each done exactly the same, and that the group repeated the whole operation on 8 separate days. How many sachets did the group fill in total?
w10_T4_003410: On Monday morning a bakery filled 9 racks with 133 bread rolls each. Before noon 298 rolls were sold at the counter. In the afternoon a cancelled order put 33 rolls back on the racks. The bakery oven holds 60 rolls at a time. The baker records proving times in minutes even though the shift plan is written in hours. That evening the same day's figures were matched at each of 7 branches, and the chain then ran 8 identical days. How many rolls did the chain handle altogether?
w10_T4_003415: On Saturday morning a market trader loaded 4 vans, each carrying 144 punnets of berries. At midday a grower added 11 punnets that had been left behind. During the afternoon a neighbouring stall passed over 71 punnets it could not sell. In the evening a cafe handed back 22 punnets. How many punnets did the trader have at the end of the day?
w10_T4_003416: Ana had 125 spare keys hanging in the caretaker's office. She handed 64 of them to new tenants. A locksmith then took 51 keys away to be recut. The office noticeboard lists 18 fire drills for the year. The keys that were left were split equally between 2 key safes, and Ana's colleague Bruno was given everything in one of them, leaving Bruno with far fewer keys than Ana had handed out that morning. 1 of Bruno's keys snapped in a lock and was thrown away. How many keys did Bruno have then?
w10_T4_003418: A theatre had 165 programmes printed for opening night, and the printer sent 38 extra ones. The box office then ordered a second run, so that the theatre held twice as many programmes as before. Each programme was afterwards bound with 4 loose inserts, and the theatre counted those inserts. The auditorium seats 900 people. A sponsor later supplied 48 further inserts for the closing night. How many inserts did the theatre have?
w10_T4_003420: On Monday morning a school library had 155 books waiting to be shelved. Later that morning a donation added 40 books to the pile. In the afternoon a class returned 25 more. In the evening the pile was shared equally between the 5 librarians on duty, and Farid took one of those equal shares. Farid then had to process his share 2 times over, once for the catalogue and once for the labels, counting one job for each book on each pass. How many processing jobs did Farid have?
w10_T4_003422: A stationery mill produced 76 reams of paper on its first shift, and the second shift produced exactly as much again, so the day's output came to double the first shift's. Each ream is split into 7 packs. Every pack holds 8 notebooks. The mill chimney is 30 metres tall. A wholesaler bought 6254 notebooks from that day's output, and 508 more were pulped after a water leak. How many notebooks from that day were left?
w10_T4_003429: A courier depot began the week with 215 sacks of post and sent 32 damaged sacks back to the sorting office. Each sack that remained holds 8 parcels. The depot then tripled its parcel count by taking on the work of a branch that had closed. Every parcel was relabelled at each of 4 stages of the network, and the depot counted one label for each pass. The depot logs its rounds in minutes even though the contract is written in hours, and its yard holds 26 vans. All of the labels were then shared equally among the 4 sorting teams, and the night team took one of those shares. How many labels did the night team handle?
